content.text:
Task (from the session that started this one):
Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin 2 is a desktop slicer with an AI agent; its server side is Kenneth's `tsd-enterprise` Django project, and its web pages are served on jusprinv2.obico.io. On 2026-11-16 an anonymous start-up report was built so the funnel can count how many downloads become a running app: the app posts to `/ent/jusprin/v2/launches` on each start and the server keeps one row per start. It was committed on side branches in both repositories and Kenneth then asked for it to be merged directly into the main checkouts with no pull requests. Two cherry-picks were started and interrupted mid-conflict. Separately, Kenneth asked whether PostHog already covers the funnel; it does not, because the PostHog snippet is only loaded on app.obico.io and JusPrin 2's pages use their own template, so he asked for PostHog on the JusPrin pages. Kenneth's rules: plain commits on `jusprin-dev` (app) and `master` (server), never merge commits, commit only when asked, push nothing, never touch other sessions' uncommitted edits in the server checkout, and ask decisions in full as "Decision needed" questions with options, costs and your pick.

Task:
Two pieces of work, in this order. Kenneth's words: "create a task chip with options to finish the cherry-picks and add posthog to the jusprin pages". Land everything as plain commits in the main checkouts, no merge commits, no pull requests, and push nothing.

Part 1: finish two cherry-picks that were interrupted mid-way. Check each checkout's state with `git status` and `git log --oneline -3` before doing anything; one of them may already be complete.

- JusPrin, main checkout `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin`, branch `jusprin-dev`. The commit being picked is `bd9d200976` ("The app tells its server once per start that it started") from branch `claude/conversion-funnel-1f5b9e`. The conflicts are in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentConfiguration.hpp` and `.cpp`: `jusprin-dev` added `cloud_error_reports_url` in the same spot where the pick adds `cloud_launches_url`. Keep both, the error-reports one first, each as its own declaration and function. If the pick already finished, confirm both helpers are present and the tree is clean. Do not build in that checkout's `build/` folder; another session may be using it. The same code was built and tested in worktree `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/conversion-funnel-1f5b9e` (`jusprin_update_tests` all pass, and a scratch app posted the report), so a compile check of the two merged files is enough: `cmake --build /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/conversion-funnel-1f5b9e/build/arm64 --config Release --target jusprin_update_tests -- -j2` after copying the resolved `AgentConfiguration.{hpp,cpp}` into that worktree, or any equivalent check that both helpers compile. Leave the untracked file `jusprin2-conversion-funnel-report.md` in the worktree alone.
- Server, main checkout `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise`, branch `master`. The commit being picked is `ed6f6540a2` ("JusPrin 2: keep one row for each start of the desktop app") from worktree `.claude/worktrees/launch-ping`, branch `claude/launch-ping`. The one conflict is `web_ent/jusprin/v2/urls.py`: `master` added the `error_reports` import and route where the pick adds `launches`. Keep both: `from . import app_errors, launches, sign_in, views, web`, and both `path(...)` lines with their comments, error_reports first. Then `GIT_EDITOR=true git cherry-pick --continue`. That checkout holds other sessions' uncommitted edits (`gateway.py`, `credits.py`, `billing.py`, `app_errors.py`, `errors.py`, `web.py`, two web templates, `lb_failures.py`, several tests, `.claude/launch.json`, and the `obico-server` submodule pointer): never stage, commit, revert or stash any of them. After the pick: `docker compose exec web python manage.py migrate jusprin` (migrations on the normal local database are allowed) and `docker compose exec web python manage.py test jusprin.v2.tests.test_launches`, both run from `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise`. All five tests must pass.

Part 2: load PostHog on the JusPrin 2 pages. Today Obico's shared layout `web_ent/app_ent/templates/layout_ent.html` inserts the PostHog browser snippet only when the host is `app.obico.io`, and identifies the signed-in person with `posthog.identify(user.id, {name, email, ...})`. JusPrin 2's pages (pricing, billing, checkout, cancel, portal) are served on `jusprinv2.obico.io` from `web_ent/jusprin/templates/jusprin/v2/web/base.html`, which does not extend that layout and loads nothing. Add the snippet to that base template so every JusPrin 2 page sends a page view, and identify the signed-in person by user id only, no email and no name. Keep the key in settings, not in the template. Before writing it, put this to Kenneth as one "Decision needed" paragraph and wait for his answer: a separate PostHog project for JusPrin 2 (its own key, events kept apart from Obico's, needs him to create the project and give you the key) or Obico's existing project (key `REDACTED` in `layout_ent.html`, nothing to create, JusPrin and Obico events mixed, filter by host). State the cost of each and your pick. Also ask whether he wants one server-side event, "app opened", sent from the account endpoint (`views.account`, called by the desktop app each time it starts while signed in), which no browser snippet can ever record; that needs the `posthog` Python library on the server and is optional. Do not add it unless he says yes. Test the page change in the normal local stack (`docker compose exec web ...`; the local site for JusPrin 2 is `jusprinv2.localhost:3334`) and show him the pricing page's HTML contains the snippet and that the identify call carries only the user id. The privacy policy already covers page views as usage of the person's own account.

Done looks like: both cherry-picks finished as plain commits on `jusprin-dev` and `master` with the tests above passing, the PostHog snippet on the JusPrin 2 pages committed on `master` after Kenneth's answers, nothing pushed, and a short report saying what landed where. Write like a colleague talking, one idea per sentence, no labels of your own invention, and when a decision is Kenneth's, ask it in full as a question starting "Decision needed".

Shared notes folder for this group of sessions (outside the repo; read siblings' notes there, leave hand-over notes or large findings there instead of pasting them into messages): /Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_dab359b6-3c58-49e3-8257-6334fb89d649

input.ask: Which PostHog project should the JusPrin 2 pages report to?

content.text:
Both cherry-picks are now plain local commits, and nothing is pushed. The PostHog change for the JusPrin 2 web pages needs two answers from you before I write it.

**What landed**

- **JusPrin, on `jusprin-dev`:** commit `2eb775ed90`, "The app tells its server once per start that it started". This pick had already finished before I started. `AgentConfiguration.hpp` and `.cpp` now have both URL helpers, `cloud_error_reports_url` first and then `cloud_launches_url`. Each is its own declaration and function, and the checkout has no uncommitted changes to tracked files.
- **Server, on `master`:** commit `158841ad99`, "JusPrin 2: keep one row for each start of the desktop app". In `urls.py` I kept both imports and both routes, with the error-reports route first. The migration `0006_app_launch` applied to the local database, and all 5 tests in `jusprin.v2.tests.test_launches` pass. No other session's uncommitted files were staged.

The local `web` container had been crash-looping. The interrupted cherry-pick had left conflict markers in `urls.py`, and the server couldn't import that file. Once the file was fixed I restarted the container, and it now reports healthy.

**Decision needed: which PostHog project the JusPrin 2 pages report to.**
- **A separate JusPrin 2 project.** JusPrin's events never mix with Obico's, and its funnels and person counts need no filtering. The cost is that you create the project in PostHog and send me its key, so the change waits on you.
- **Obico's existing project.** It uses the key already in `layout_ent.html`, and there is nothing to create, so I can build it now. The cost is that JusPrin and Obico events land together. Every JusPrin chart then needs a filter on the host `jusprinv2.obico.io`. Also, one person with an Obico account and a JusPrin 2 account shows up as two different people, because the two accounts have different user ids.

My pick is the separate project, because a funnel you have to remember to filter is easy to get wrong. Which do you want?

**Decision needed: should the server also send an "app opened" event?**
A browser snippet only records the web pages. It never sees the desktop app start. I could send one server-side event to PostHog from the account endpoint, which the signed-in app calls to show the credit balance. That needs the `posthog` Python library added to the server. One correction to the brief: the app calls that endpoint more than once per start, from Home and again when the AI panel refreshes. So the event would really mean "a signed-in person used the app". PostHog's daily and weekly active-user counts would still be right, but a raw event count would overstate how many times the app started. The anonymous start-up report you just landed already counts starts, signed in or not. My pick is to skip the server event for now and add it later if you want signed-in activity in PostHog. Do you want it?

**Two things I'll handle once you answer**
- The JusPrin 2 page template, `base.html`, has another session's uncommitted edit: it removes the `.alert` style. I'll commit only my own lines and leave that edit uncommitted.
- That template says the pages use no script. I'll update that note, because the PostHog snippet is a script.

The search covered project and billing rules but didn't address whether funnels can span projects.

- **Free plan limit:** The free plan allows one project. PostHog has two plans: Free — No credit card required. Paid plans include more projects (6 on pay-as-you-go), and Boost and higher platform packages offer unlimited projects.
- **Shared allowance:** Billing is per organization, not per project. Usage from all projects is combined under one free allowance, so adding projects does not add free usage. One docs example says three projects each sending 400,000 events count as 1.2 million events against one free tier.
- **Recommended setup:** PostHog suggests separate projects for local development, staging, and production, which is why the free plan's single project blocks that setup.
- **Older forum claims:** A forum thread from several years ago says free limits apply per organization. A different forum post says a second environment requires a card even within free limits. Both are older than the current docs, so treat them as dated.
- **Funnels across projects:** None of the results mention cross-project funnels or whether a funnel can combine data from two projects. The product docs or a direct PostHog search would be needed to confirm that.

input.ask: Use Obico's existing PostHog project for the JusPrin 2 pages?

content.text:
Your concern is right: a separate project can never link an obico.io visit to a JusPrin billing page view, because a PostHog funnel works inside one project. I'd expect that from how PostHog stores data, but its docs don't say it directly. But I checked, and a single project doesn't give you that funnel today either. That's for two reasons:

- **obico.io sends nothing to PostHog.** Its pages load only Google Tag Manager, and that container has no tags in it. The JusPrin page at obico.io/jusprin.html loads nothing at all.
- **Most billing pages open inside the app, not the browser.** The JusPrin 2 app shows pricing and billing in its own web view, which keeps cookies apart from the person's Chrome or Safari. Someone who browses obico.io in Chrome and then opens pricing in the app looks like two different visitors, even in one project.

The link is still possible in one project. The browser just has to learn who the person is. That happens when a page on jusprinv2.obico.io tells PostHog the user id in the person's real browser. Two such moments exist today: the "Open in browser" button on the billing page, and, I believe, Google sign-in, which opens a page in the browser. PostHog shares its anonymous id across obico.io subdomains, so it would join that person's earlier obico.io visits to their account. That's PostHog's default cookie setting, which I haven't checked against our setup. The JusPrin pages inside the app identify the same user id, so the whole path joins up. That needs two extra steps: PostHog on obico.io, and the snippet on the sign-in page too. With a separate project, no amount of extra work gets you this.

**A separate project**
- Pro: JusPrin's numbers need no filter. Obico's dashboards stay as they are.
- Con: no funnel from obico.io, ever.
- Con: PostHog's free plan allows only one project. The pay-as-you-go plan allows six. Billing is per organization either way, so a second project doesn't add any free event allowance.
- Con: you have to create it and send me the key.

**Obico's project**
- Pro: the obico.io-to-billing funnel becomes possible once the two extra steps are done.
- Pro: nothing to create or pay for.
- Con: every JusPrin chart needs a filter on the host jusprinv2.obico.io.
- Con: someone with both an Obico account and a JusPrin 2 account counts as two people, because the two accounts have different user ids.

Given your funnel, I now pick Obico's project. The filtering is a small cost next to losing that funnel for good. My earlier pick ignored it.

Your other answer is still open: should the server send an "app opened" event to PostHog from the account endpoint? My pick is still no for now. That endpoint is called several times per start, and the start-up report you just landed already counts starts.

Sources:
- [PostHog pricing](https://posthog.com/pricing)
- [PostHog billing questions](https://posthog.com/docs/billing/common-questions)
- [PostHog projects](https://posthog.com/docs/settings/projects)
